data.why: scripts/demo-data.py (committed in the repo) drives the app's own routes to build a realistic lab (Rivera Lab) with racks, mice, litters, strains, plasmids and inventories, which is exactly what the app expects and far richer than hand-written fixtures.

goals: log a new litter's birth and walk it through weaning and the genotyping queue
set up a mating in the breeders list and track which cage it returns to
add a new mouse strain and place incoming animals into a rack position
record an experiment's manipulation and body weights, and read off the chart whether treatment and control groups differ
check which reagents and antibodies are expired or low in the lab inventory and reorder them
upload a plasmid sequence file and inspect its features on the interactive map

review.summary: The tree is accurate and well grounded: every screen I sampled shows what its node claims, and the breeding, experiment, inventory and plasmid stages are sensibly structured, with mostly tool-free general labels. It needs fixes before filing: several of the plan's own goals are unfinished (genotyping results, sequence upload, a real group comparison), calendar/notebook and the multi-organism side are missing, and the independent check never got past login, so nothing has been replayed.
